title: API 653 Training in St. Louis: Tank Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 653 exam prep for St. Louis tank inspectors: Hartford and Wood River tank farms, ethanol and asphalt service, SPCC and PHMSA rules, self-paced online.
h1: API 653 training in St. Louis: exam preparation for aboveground storage tank inspectors at Hartford terminals, the Wood River refinery and the Illinois pipeline hub
html:
API 653 exam prep for tank inspectors in the St. Louis region

Storage around St. Louis gathers where pipelines meet the refinery and the river. Hartford, Wood River and Roxana, on the Illinois side in Madison County, hold refinery tank fields, products and ethanol terminals and pipeline tank farms; Patoka, the crude hub to the east, is tied to Wood River by pipe; and the Missouri bank has products storage too. Every one of those tanks needs external and internal inspections, floor and settlement evaluation, and somebody who can decide on repairs, alterations, reconstruction and the height to which it may be filled. The API 653 Aboveground Storage Tank Inspector certification is built around those decisions.

Atlantis NDT's API 653 course prepares you for the examination: it is self-paced and online, and an instructor answers your questions as you go. There is no Atlantis classroom in St. Louis or in the Metro East; Atlantis's offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. API sets eligibility, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification, and each candidate applies to API directly.

Tank farms around St. Louis, in the operators' own documents

SiteWhat the operator or EIA publishesAPI 653 work it generates
Kinder Morgan Wood River Terminal, 1000 BP Lane, Hartford, Illinois21 tanks holding 1,947,578 barrels, from 48,577 to 204,584 barrels each; petroleum and ethanol; Marathon, Explorer and Phillips 66 listed as receiving pipelines; truck loading and unloadingShells, floors, roofs and nozzles on large products and ethanol tanks
Explorer Pipeline at Wood RiverDescribed in the December 2024 revision of Explorer's shipper manual as a mainline pump site with a receiving tank farmPipeline tankage, which PHMSA regulates as breakout tanks where it meets the federal definition
Wood River refinery, RoxanaEIA's 2026 report: 345,000 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation and 26,000 barrels per stream day of asphalt and road oil production capacityCrude, intermediate and product tanks, and asphalt storage, which is normally heated
Wood River to PatokaMarathon Pipe Line's Wood River-to-Patoka pipeline, which MPLX announced in 2017 it would expand; Enbridge's planned 56-mile Southern Illinois Connector on the same route, expected in service in 2028Oil moving east to Patoka, which Enbridge says connects onward to the Gulf Coast
Buckeye, North St. LouisListed under Missouri in Buckeye's 2024 directory of connecting facilities as the North St. Louis Terminal of Buckeye Terminals, LLCProducts storage on the Missouri bank

Figures are the publishers' own. The Kinder Morgan terminal sheet carries no date, the Explorer and Buckeye documents are from 2024, and EIA's report describes refineries as of January 2026. EIA still lists Wood River under the WRB Refining partnership, half Phillips 66 and half Cenovus, although Phillips 66 reports completing its purchase of the Cenovus half in October 2025.

Ethanol, asphalt and crude: the damage mechanism list, read locally

For the March, July and November 2027 windows, the API 653 effectivity sheet limits API RP 571 to its terms and definitions and ten mechanisms. Several match St. Louis storage closely:

  • 3.28 Ethanol stress corrosion cracking. The Hartford terminal handles ethanol, and fuel-grade ethanol can crack stressed carbon steel, so learn the conditions RP 571 associates with it and the places on a tank and its fittings where it tends to appear.
  • 3.57 Soil corrosion, 3.45 microbiologically influenced corrosion and 3.19 concentration cell corrosion. The underside of a floor, the water and sludge layer on top of it, and crevices under deposits are where crude and products tanks lose metal.
  • 3.22 Corrosion under insulation. Insulated, heated shells such as asphalt tanks are the obvious candidates, especially where insulation is damaged at nozzles, stiffeners and the shell-to-roof joint.
  • 3.11 Brittle fracture. API 653's brittle fracture assessment exists for older tanks of uncertain toughness, and a Midwest winter makes it a practical question rather than a theoretical one.
  • 3.14 and 3.15 caustic corrosion and caustic stress corrosion cracking, and 3.62 sulfuric acid corrosion. Chemical storage at refineries and plants, where caustic or acid is kept for treating and process use.
  • 3.8 Atmospheric corrosion on roofs, shells and structural steel, which every outdoor tank faces.

Questions are drawn from the RP 571 paragraphs, not from site experience, so read the listed sections carefully even for mechanisms you see at work.

The editions on the 2027 effectivity sheet

The same sheet names the publications for those three windows. Study these editions, not whatever is on the shelf at your terminal:

  • API 653, fifth edition (November 2014), with Addenda 1 to 4, the latest dated July 2025, and Errata 1 and 2;
  • API 650, fourteenth edition (August 2025);
  • API RP 575, fifth edition (September 2024), with Addendum 1 (July 2025) and Addendum 2 (June 2026);
  • API RP 651, fifth edition (August 2024), on cathodic protection, and API RP 652, sixth edition (December 2025), on bottom linings;
  • API RP 576, only its sections 4.3.2 and 6.7, and API RP 577, third edition, with Errata 1;
  • the 2025 edition of ASME Section V, Articles 1, 2, 6, 7 and 23 (SE-797 only), and Section IX for welding only.

The Body of Knowledge adds that some jurisdictions write older editions into their own rules, and that the examination still follows the sheet.

Which rules bring an API 653 inspector to a Metro East tank

EPA spill prevention rules

Under the SPCC rule at 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6), aboveground bulk storage containers at onshore facilities other than oil production facilities need integrity testing on a regular schedule following industry standards. EPA's fact sheet on the requirement names API 653 and STI SP001 as commonly used standards, says that once a plan adopts a standard the relevant parts of it are mandatory, and notes that trained facility staff can often make the frequent visual walk-arounds, while for field-erected tanks inspected under API 653 the formal inspections are to be conducted by an API 653 certified inspector.

PHMSA breakout tanks

At pipeline tank farms, 49 CFR 195.432 governs. Its general requirement for an inspection at least once each calendar year, at intervals not exceeding 15 months, applies except to tanks inspected under paragraphs (b) and (c). Paragraph (b) requires atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks to be inspected to API 653, excluding API 653's risk-based alternative for setting the internal interval; paragraph (c) sends tanks built to API 2510 to section 6 of API 510. PHMSA proposed in 2026 to allow risk-based internal intervals for breakout tanks, but that remains a proposal rather than a final rule.

Illinois fire and tank rules

Illinois's own storage tank and fire code requirements apply on top of the federal rules. The Chicago page for this course sets them out, so this page does not repeat them.

Worked example: the bottom course of a relocated tank

Tanks are sometimes dismantled at one site and rebuilt at another. API 653 sends the shell design of a reconstructed tank back to API 650, and the Body of Knowledge expects candidates to calculate the design and hydrostatic test thicknesses by API 650's one-foot method, which applies to tanks of 200 ft diameter and smaller. Suppose a 60 ft diameter products tank is re-erected with a design liquid level of 40 ft, a product specific gravity of 0.85 and a corrosion allowance of 1/16 in. The problem gives Sd = 23,200 psi and St = 24,900 psi for the plate.

  1. Design thickness of the bottom course: td = 2.6 D (H − 1) G ÷ Sd + CA = 2.6 × 60 × 39 × 0.85 ÷ 23,200 + 0.0625 = 5,171.4 ÷ 23,200 + 0.0625 = 0.223 + 0.0625 = 0.285 in.
  2. Hydrostatic test thickness: tt = 2.6 D (H − 1) ÷ St = 6,084 ÷ 24,900 = 0.244 in. G drops out because the test is made with water.
  3. The larger figure, 0.285 in., governs. Reused 5/16 in. plate measuring 0.300 in. at its thinnest passes; a plate already down to 0.280 in. does not.
  4. The second course, whose bottom sits 8 ft higher (H = 32 ft), needs td = 2.6 × 60 × 31 × 0.85 ÷ 23,200 + 0.0625 = 0.240 in. and tt = 0.194 in. API 650 also never lets a shell course be thinner than the minimum nominal thickness for the diameter, 1/4 in. from 50 ft up to but not including 120 ft, so under API 650 that figure governs; read whether a reconstruction question wants the calculated thickness or the plate API 650 requires.

The common slips are using H instead of H − 1, adding the corrosion allowance to the test thickness, and overlooking API 650's minimum nominal thickness on the upper courses.

Floors, foundations and cathodic protection near the river

Much of the region's storage stands close to the Mississippi, and floors and foundations are where tank inspection gets most of its work. Magnetic flux leakage floor scans find underside loss; settlement surveys and the evaluation methods in API 653's Annex B judge whether the shell and bottom have moved beyond what the standard allows; and RP 651 and RP 652, both on the 2027 sheet, cover cathodic protection of tank bottoms and internal linings. A candidate who has scanned floors or reviewed CP readings will recognise these chapters, but should still learn how API 653 converts the findings into a minimum bottom thickness and the next internal inspection date.

Routes into API 653 for St. Louis tank people

API counts education plus experience in the last ten years, gained while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency, under Annex D of API 653. The usual local starting points:

  • Floor scanning and UT technicians who survey tanks for contractors at Hartford and Wood River; ASNT SNT-TC-1A training is on the St. Louis NDT training page.
  • Tank welders, erectors and repair crews, whose construction and repair time counts on the two-year, high-school and no-formal-education routes as long as a year is spent supervising or performing inspection. Some also prepare for AWS CWI in St. Louis.
  • Terminal operators and maintenance staff moving into a tank inspection role.
  • Engineers with a bachelor's degree, who need one year of supervising or performing tank inspection.

The API 653 certification page sets out each route in detail.

Studying API 653 between terminal outages

Tank work follows each owner's outage schedule, which often leaves some months far busier than others. Use the quieter months for the heaviest reading, which is API 653 itself and the parts of API 650 that it borrows. Then work the calculations the Body of Knowledge lists: corrosion rates and intervals, joint efficiency, fill height, weld sizes at openings, hot tap spacing, settlement and the number of survey points, impact testing, existing and reconstructed shell thickness, and corroded area evaluation. Because the course is self-paced, you can stop during an outage and pick up where you left off, and send the instructor the questions the outage raises. The examination is 170 questions over a long day, closed-book first and open-book after lunch. Prometric lists test centres in and around St. Louis; book a seat soon after API accepts you.

Sponsoring tank inspectors from a Hartford terminal or a St. Louis contractor

Terminals and contractors often want several API 653 inspectors at once. A group enquiry is welcome and fees are quoted on request, while API treats each candidate separately from application to result. For background reading, see the API 653 tank inspection guide. In the US, Atlantis performs UT, MT, PT and VT inspection, with local detail on the St. Louis tank inspection page; it does not perform radiography.

faq.q: Is there an API 653 class I can attend in St. Louis or Hartford?
faq.a: Not with Atlantis. There is no Atlantis classroom in the St. Louis area; the API 653 course is online and self-paced, with an instructor answering your questions, and you begin when you enrol. Some other providers run seminars on fixed dates, and some terminal operators train their own staff. Whichever route you take, API's examination is sat in person at a Prometric test centre after your application has been accepted.

faq.q: Does the API 653 exam cover ethanol stress corrosion cracking, given the ethanol stored at Hartford?
faq.a: Yes, for the March, July and November 2027 windows. Their effectivity sheet includes RP 571 paragraph 3.28, ethanol stress corrosion cracking, among the ten mechanisms examined, together with soil corrosion, microbiologically influenced corrosion, sulfuric acid corrosion and others. That is directly useful at terminals such as Hartford, which handle ethanol. Check the sheet for your own window, because API revises the list from time to time.

faq.q: Do breakout tanks at a Wood River pipeline tank farm follow the same rules as refinery tanks?
faq.a: Not quite. Atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks fall under 49 CFR 195.432, which requires inspection to API 653 but excludes its risk-based alternative for setting the internal inspection interval. Refinery tanks are usually inspected under the owner's programme, often alongside the EPA SPCC rule. PHMSA proposed in 2026 to relax the breakout tank restriction, but at the time of writing it was a proposal, not a final rule.

faq.q: Under SPCC, who may do the routine visual checks and who must do the formal inspection?
faq.a: EPA's fact sheet on integrity testing says trained facility staff can often perform the frequent visual walk-arounds, while regular integrity testing may need specialists; for field-erected tanks under API 653, it says formal inspections are to be conducted by an API 653 certified inspector. The owner's SPCC Plan should record which standard applies, the schedule and the personnel qualifications. That is one of the main reasons terminals want certified inspectors on staff.

faq.q: I build and repair tanks around St. Louis. Does that time count toward API 653?
faq.a: It can. For the two-year degree, high-school and no-formal-education routes, API counts experience in the design, fabrication, repair, operation or inspection of aboveground storage tanks, provided at least one year of it was spent supervising or performing inspection as API 653 describes. The experience must fall within the last ten years and be gained while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency. API verifies what you declare.

faq.q: Which API 650 edition should a St. Louis candidate study for API 653?
faq.a: For the March, July and November 2027 windows, the effectivity sheet lists the fourteenth edition of API 650, published in August 2025, alongside API 653's fifth edition with its addenda. Many tanks in service were built to much older editions, and some state rules cite older documents, but the examination follows the sheet. The course study plan is built on the sheet for the window you choose.

faq.q: Do I need to study cathodic protection and bottom linings for the exam?
faq.a: Yes. RP 651 on cathodic protection of aboveground petroleum storage tanks and RP 652 on linings of tank bottoms are both on the 2027 effectivity sheet, in their fifth and sixth editions respectively. The Body of Knowledge limits RP 651 to sections 1 to 6, 8 and 11 and leaves cathodic protection system design and interference currents out of the exam; for RP 652 it lists lining types, when a lining is recommended, why linings fail and lining materials. Read both alongside the floor sections of API 653.

faq.q: Can a Hartford terminal enrol several tank inspectors at once?
faq.a: Yes. One enquiry can cover all your candidates; tell us how many there are and which windows they are aiming for, and the quote covers the group. Each person studies at their own pace with the instructor available, and each applies to API and sits the examination separately. Spreading candidates across windows can help a terminal keep cover during its outage season.
